commands: bun -e 'const glob = new Bun.Glob("**/*"); let count = 0; for await (const p of glob.scan({ cwd: ".", onlyFiles: true })) if (!p.split("/").includes(".git")) count++; if (count >= 180) throw new Error(String(count))'

notes: This focused config measures Brainstorm narrowing behavior separately from the four-route plugin baseline.
Every scenario runs through a read-only isolated Pi Agent and should leave no Spec, Plan, CONTEXT.md, or implementation edit.
Launch all five scenarios in one parallel batch with antigravity/gemini-3.6-flash.
Record provider billing cost as unavailable_by_host; do not estimate it.

scenarios.title: Ask only the current blocking question
scenarios.purpose: Verify that Brainstorm resolves dependent decisions one branch at a time without adopting full Grill Mode for an ordinary task.
scenarios.userInput: Use the local Pi Skill `imm-brainstorm` to frame this request in the fixture workspace: improve account cancellation. Whether data retention needs discussion depends entirely on whether cancellation means ending a subscription or deleting the account. Inspect only CONTEXT.md, README.md, and docs/solutions first. Ask only the current highest-value blocking question; do not ask downstream retention questions yet. Do not create or edit any files.
successChecklist: The response asks exactly one narrowing question about the meaning of cancellation.
The response does not ask a downstream data-retention question in the same turn.
The response remains a concise Brainstorm interaction and does not route to Planner or Preplan.
No workspace file is created or changed.

scenarios.title: Keep independent probes inside the lightweight budget
scenarios.purpose: Verify that independent ambiguities can be surfaced together without turning every Brainstorm into serial questioning.
scenarios.userInput: Use the local Pi Skill `imm-brainstorm` to frame a lightweight internal status dashboard. The intended audience and the measurable success target are both missing, but either answer can be decided independently. Inspect only CONTEXT.md and README.md first. Ask the necessary independent questions together, staying within the lightweight probe budget. Do not create or edit any files.
successChecklist: The response asks about both intended audience and measurable success target.
The response asks no more than two narrowing questions.
The response does not force a concrete edge-case scenario or full Grill Mode.
No workspace file is created or changed.

scenarios.title: Use one discriminating lifecycle scenario
scenarios.purpose: Verify that a concrete scenario replaces a generic probe when it is the clearest way to distinguish a lifecycle boundary.
scenarios.userInput: Use the local Pi Skill `imm-brainstorm` to frame a `pause workspace` feature. It is unclear whether people with an already-open session may keep working after an admin pauses the workspace. Inspect only CONTEXT.md and README.md first. Use one concrete user scenario to clarify the lifecycle boundary, replacing a lower-value generic question rather than adding more questions. Do not create or edit any files.
successChecklist: The response asks a concrete scenario question involving an already-open session and an admin pause.
The scenario distinguishes the lifecycle or scope boundary instead of requesting generic implementation detail.
The response stays within the lightweight probe budget and does not add an exhaustive edge-case checklist.
No workspace file is created or changed.

scenarios.title: Do not invent a scenario for a complete frame
scenarios.purpose: Verify that the new scenario-gap option does not create ceremony when the request already defines behavior, scope, and success.
scenarios.userInput: Use the local Pi Skill `imm-brainstorm` to frame this already-specific request: add an admin-only CSV export button that downloads exactly the rows visible on the current page; no background jobs, no hidden columns, and success means the downloaded CSV matches the visible table order. Summarize the direction and request confirmation without inventing additional narrowing or scenario questions. Do not create or edit any files.
successChecklist: The response summarizes the specified direction without a new scenario probe.
The only question is the required confirmation request, not an invented narrowing question.
The response does not route to Planner before confirmation.
No workspace file is created or changed.

scenarios.title: Keep an unmet rejected decision closed
scenarios.purpose: Verify that recorded reconsideration conditions prevent generic re-litigation when repository evidence has not changed.
scenarios.userInput: Use the local Pi Skill `imm-brainstorm` to frame a proposal for a shared generic dispatcher in this fixture. Inspect docs/solutions/rejected-generic-dispatcher.md plus CONTEXT.md and README.md. The fixture still has only one host adapter and no repeated dispatch drift. Apply the recorded rejection and reconsider_if conditions; do not ask a generic `what changed?` question when no condition is met. Do not create or edit any files.
successChecklist: The response treats the generic dispatcher as a current constraint or non-goal.
The response cites the unmet reconsideration evidence instead of reopening the decision.
The response asks no generic `what changed?` question and does not route to Planner.
No workspace file is created or changed.
